clue.text: Established Oriental and French wine turnover last month

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for East, the Orient
vin is the French word for wine

indicators.note: a turnover flips the month's short name so it is read backwards

parts.note: December, the year's last month, is abbreviated Dec

explanation.surface: Someone sorts out an Eastern and French wine sale figure for last month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' reads like a sales term but signals a reversal. 'Established' is a past-tense verb meaning shown or proved, as evidence establishes a fact.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to show or demonstrate, so something evinced has been made plain or proved.

clue.text: Certainly not slow to speak

definitions.meaning: fast, like a train or post service that goes direct
to put into words or voice

explanation.surface: Definitely in no hurry to talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A fast train or delivery bears the name, and to voice a thought is likewise to state it.

clue.text: Realise it may be different for an old tribesman

indicators.note: may be different invites the letters of the preceding words to change their order

explanation.surface: Realise that an ancient tribe member might be different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be different' rearranges REALISE IT; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelve tribes of the ancient Hebrew people descend from Jacob, called Israel.

clue.text: Many Scots long to be a big noise!

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
lang is the Scots word for long, as in auld lang syne

explanation.surface: Lots of Scots yearn to make an impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'long' looks like a verb meaning yearn but is the adjective in Scots dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud ringing metallic sound is a big noise, as from a bell or dropped pan.

clue.text: They're put across in round figures

definitions.text: They're put across in round figures

parts.words: They're put across in round figures
parts.note: lines drawn straight across circles through the centre, not approximate numbers

explanation.definitionFit: These lines measure the width of a circle by passing through its middle.

clue.text: Uninhibited individual finding entertainment substandard

parts.note: a show is a piece of entertainment
food or a performance that is off is below par

explanation.surface: A carefree person discovers that a show was poor.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who flaunts themselves without restraint is a common description of an exhibitionist.

clue.text: Make-up wins a lover

indicators.note: make-up as in making up the letters of the following words into something new

explanation.surface: Cosmetics win over a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' rearranges WINS A.
explanation.definitionFit: A swain is a poetic word for a young suitor or boyfriend.

clue.text: Being candid about relation's employment

indicators.note: about means the word for candid goes round the word for relation

parts.note: being open is being frank and candid
a ratio is a numerical relation between quantities

explanation.surface: Someone honest about a relative's job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' means the candid word is wrapped round the relation word; 'Being' and the possessive are links. 'relation' here is the mathematical sense, not a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is the use or working of something, as a machine in use.

clue.text: Foreign character taking part in some game or other

indicators.note: taking part in signals that the answer is a part lodged inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A foreigner joins in some game or other.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in sOME GAme; 'or other' completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The last letter of the Greek alphabet is a character from a foreign script.

clue.text: Thickhead's embonpoint

parts.note: fat means thick, as a fat book
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A dimwit's plumpness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thickhead' looks like a dunce but splits as Thick + head; 'embonpoint' is a polite word for stoutness.
explanation.definitionFit: Embonpoint is a French-derived euphemism for plumpness of figure.

clue.text: Right held by parents in Italy

indicators.note: held by means the letter for right sits inside the word for the parents

parts.note: PA and MA are familiar words for father and mother

explanation.surface: A legal right is kept by a mother and father living in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a little loose: the answer is a city found in Italy, so 'in Italy' stands for a place there.
explanation.definitionFit: Parma is a northern city of the country, famous for ham and cheese.

clue.text: Getting badly beat means humiliation

indicators.note: getting badly suggests the letters of the following words are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Being beaten badly is a humiliating experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting badly' rearranges the nine letters of BEAT MEANS.
explanation.definitionFit: To abase someone is to lower or degrade them, so the state of being lowered is humiliation.

clue.text: Never leaves off!

parts.note: read as never taking its leaves off: a plant or tree that keeps its foliage all year round

explanation.definitionFit: A tree that keeps green foliage through winter never sheds its leaves, a botanical pun on ceasing.

clue.text: For the present time it's 21

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, labels the present era of the calendar
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: For now, it is the motto that counts.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 refers to the answer at 21 across, MOTTO; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto and a saying are both short memorable phrases expressing a principle.

clue.text: Projector with an arm-rest

definitions.meaning: a device that hurls stones, like David's weapon against Goliath
a cloth support hung from the neck to rest an injured arm

explanation.surface: A film projector comes with somewhere to rest your arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a strap for hurling stones and a bandage loop cradling a broken arm.

clue.text: Discovering corruption in an order, he's choked

indicators.note: in means the word for corruption goes within the order's name

parts.note: the Garter is the senior order of English knighthood
rot is decay or corruption

explanation.surface: Finding corruption in a knightly order, he is lost for words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovering' is a link. 'he's choked' reads as upset but means he has strangled someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler is one who has throttled a victim, typically with a cord.

clue.text: People asking questions of pitmen following cut-back

indicators.note: following means the word for pitmen comes after the reversed piece
back with cut means the word for cut is read backwards

parts.note: to axe is to cut
miners work in pits

explanation.surface: Interviewers question coal miners after cutbacks at the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut-back' looks like one noun but splits: 'back' turns the word for cut round, and 'following' places the pitmen after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Examiners set papers and ask questions to test candidates.

clue.text: The eccentric can rage or bluster

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or odd, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The oddball may fly into a rage or rant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges CAN RAGE OR; 'The' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluster is swaggering, boastful talk typical of haughty self-importance.

clue.text: No longer in accord over a charge, that's clear

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
at one means in accord, giving one
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: No longer agreeing on a fee, that much is obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text says 'dear'; the scan shows 'clear', the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to clear someone of blame or a charge.

clue.text: The growth in gold was good for the speculator!

indicators.note: in means the word for growth goes inside the heraldic word for gold

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
a rise is an increase or growth

explanation.surface: A rise in the gold price pleased the investor who had gambled on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was good for' is a link phrase; the speculator here is one who speculates in ideas, a theorist.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who forms theories is speculating, guessing at explanations without proof.

clue.text: Modify a painting technique

parts.note: to temper is to moderate or modify

explanation.surface: Change a method of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera uses pigment mixed with egg yolk, a painting method of the Renaissance.

clue.text: 23 dn can set one so at odds

indicators.note: at odds means the letters are in disagreement with their order and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A trap can be set, with the odds against escape.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 dn is SNARE; 'at odds' rearranges ONE SO, and 'can set' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop of rope that tightens is a classic trap for animals.

clue.text: Life is real! Life is —!" (Longfellow)

parts.note: fill in the missing word from Longfellow's A Psalm of Life

explanation.definitionFit: The line from A Psalm of Life continues with a word meaning serious and sincere.

clue.text: Saw non-drinker in low accommodation

indicators.note: in tells us the teetotal letters go inside the cow's sound
accommodation means the cow's sound houses the non-drinker's letters

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
TT stands for teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: A tool found by a teetotaller in cheap lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is not the tool or the verb but a noun meaning a saying; 'low' is the cow's call, not 'cheap'.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw in the old sense is a proverb or maxim, a short wise saying.

clue.text: A link that is apparent in deposit being raised

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for that is sits inside the other piece
in a down clue being raised turns the word for deposit upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: to put is to deposit, set down
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A connection becomes clear when a deposit is increased.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being raised' turns the deposit word upward, as a down clue reads; 'in' puts the abbreviation for that is inside; 'apparent' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-up is a connection or merger between two parties.

clue.text: A person looking around needs spectacles always

parts.note: sights are spectacles, things worth seeing
e'er is the poetic short form of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Someone peering about always needs glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spectacles' looks like glasses but means sights.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist goes around viewing the notable places of a town.

clue.text: Points are given for 19

parts.note: S and N are compass points, south and north

explanation.surface: Points are awarded for answer 19.
explanation.walkthrough: 19 is NOOSE, at 19 across; 'given for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose and a trap are both devices for catching animals.

clue.text: Board's report about bad start

indicators.note: about means the word for report goes round the first letter of bad

parts.note: a tale is a story or report

indicators.note: start means the opening letter of the word bad

explanation.surface: The committee's account deals with a poor beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board's' reads as 'board is', so the definition is Board.
explanation.definitionFit: A table is a board for meals, and a table also means a board of figures.

clue.text: Observes focus is an optical problem

parts.note: to eye is to observe
to train a camera or gaze is to focus it

explanation.surface: Watching and concentrating hard can be a problem for your vision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired, aching eyes from overuse are a common complaint of vision.

clue.text: Trains one or two

definitions.meaning: something that trains, as an orthodontic device trains crooked teeth straight
a pair, especially of game birds shot

explanation.surface: A railway passenger wants one train or perhaps two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is a link between the two definitions; 'Trains' is a verb, not railway carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: A dental appliance straightens teeth over time, and the same word means a pair of pheasants.

clue.text: Attack when alone

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he left'
per se is Latin for by itself, alone

explanation.surface: Strike when you are on your own.
explanation.definitionFit: To asperse is to slander, attacking someone's reputation.

clue.text: The section empowered to supply heating

definitions.meaning: a part or component of a whole
the electrically powered coil in a kettle or heater

explanation.surface: The part of the system given power to provide warmth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empowered' is a pun on being supplied with electric power.
explanation.definitionFit: A component of anything is one of its parts, and a heater's electric coil bears the same name.
